pr_title: Fix KeyInfoX509Data encoding negative serial numbers
pr_body:
.NET Framework treats the serial number from an X509Certificate as unsigned, and encodes the serial number as a positive integer. This changes the managed implementation to encode the serial number in the same way.

Fixes #91064
pr_comments: Test failures are unrelated. New test passed in both NetFx and NetCore runs. Merging.

issue_context.title: EncryptedXml fails to decrypt element encrypted by a X509 certificate referenced by a negative issuer serial
comments:
This is a regression from .NET Framework 4.8, so for consistency purposes I think we should address this in .NET 9.

Given that negative serial numbers are non-conformant, (RFC 5280, 4.1.2.2) I don't think we need to fix this for .NET 8, and also there is a work around posted in the original issue.

Additionally, thank you for posting an excellent report with full steps to reproduce the issue.

Okay, so I finally got around to looking at this, and this appears to have been broken a long time ago in https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/pull/14662.

The problem is not with decrypting - the problem is with encrypting. Rather, when you encrypt, it write down the serial number as `<X509SerialNumber>-85070591730234615865843651857942052863</X509SerialNumber>`, whereas .NET Framework writes it down as `<X509SerialNumber>255211775190703847597530955573826158593</X509SerialNumber>`.

We should change the encoding in `KeyInfoX509Data` to work the same as .NET Framework.

review_comments: Since this is an uncommon path, and needs to work in .NET Standard, I didn't think it was worthwhile to special-case NETCOREAPP which gives us `isUnsigned`.
